title_en: Li Chuanxiong — Application for Public Summons for Exhortation for Lost Stock Certificates
keywords_en: Civil; Public Summons for Exhortation; First Instance; Primary People's Court; Shanghai Municipality; Natural Person; Civil Procedure Law; Public Summons for Exhortation for Lost Stock Certificates; No One Claims Rights; Support the Plaintiff; Loss of Stock Certificates; Theft; Securities
full_text_en:
Li Chuanxiong – Application for Public Summons for Lost Shares

Applicant: Li Chuanxiong, male, 68 years old, a retired worker of the Passenger Fleet of Shanghai Maritime Administration.

In April 1986, Li Chuanxiong purchased 60 A shares (each share face value RMB 100) of Shanghai Vacuum Electronic Device Co., Ltd. from Shanghai Shenyin Securities Company, with stock numbers 9115 to 9174. In September 1991, while Li Chuanxiong was accompanying his wife to see a doctor, a thief broke into his home and stole all the aforementioned shares. Upon discovering the burglary, Li Chuanxiong immediately reported to the public security authorities and reported the loss to the stock exchange. Subsequently, the theft case was solved by the public security authorities, but the said shares had been destroyed by the criminal. At that time, the Shanghai stock market transaction had shifted from physical share certificates to paperless trading, and shareholders were required to have their shares recorded in the computer system. Because Li's shares had been lost, the securities company refused to handle the computer recording procedures. In February 1993, Li Chuanxiong obtained an application form for reissuance of lost shares from Shanghai Vacuum Electronic Device Co., Ltd., and made a declaration of lost shares at the Jing'an District Notary Public Office of Shanghai. In June 1993, Li Chuanxiong filed an application with the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai for public summons for lost shares.

Pursuant to the principle of Article 193 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai High People's Court designated the Jing'an District People's Court to accept the case.

The Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to the designation by the Shanghai High People's Court and with reference to Article 193 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, decided to accept Li Chuanxiong's application. Upon verification with the Registration Department of the Shanghai Stock Exchange, it was confirmed that the applicant Li Chuanxiong did own 60 A shares (each share face value RMB 100) of Shanghai Vacuum Electronic Device Co., Ltd. Within three days after accepting the case, i.e., on June 12, 1993, the court issued a public notice, and published the content in the *Shanghai Securities News* on June 15, urging interested parties to claim their rights within 60 days. During the period of public summons, no one came forward to claim rights. After the expiration of the period, Li Chuanxiong applied to the Jing'an District People's Court for a judgment on August 18 of the same year.

Pursuant to the application of Li Chuanxiong, and with reference to Article 197 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai rendered a judgment on September 22, 1993:

1. Declare that the 60 A shares of Shanghai Vacuum Electronic Device Co., Ltd. (each share face value RMB 100, stock numbers 9115 to 9174) lost by the applicant Li Chuanxiong are void.

2. From the date of announcement of this judgment, the applicant Li Chuanxiong shall have the right to apply to the issuing company, Shanghai Vacuum Electronic Device Co., Ltd., for reissuance.
